dedupe_keys.name: nlr dsgrid demand side grid toolkit bottom up hourly us electricity load by county sector and end use

description: dsgrid is the National Laboratory of the Rockies (formerly NREL) demand-side grid toolkit for building electricity load data sets at high temporal, geographic, sectoral and end-use resolution for power system analysis. Contents: a bottom-up method that combines detailed sector models (ResStock for homes, ComStock for commercial buildings, TEMPO for transportation including county-level light-duty EV charging, and industrial energy methods) to give hourly load time series by subsector, end use and US county, each typically covering a full historical or future model year; the sector models also give other fuel use such as natural gas. Load data are time-synchronised with solar and wind data sets, and dsgrid-flex turns device-level load into aggregated flexibility resources for managed charging studies. Producer: NLR Energy Systems Analysis. Coverage: United States, by county. Format and access: open source code on GitHub (dsgrid and project repositories such as the Standard Scenarios TEMPO project) and data sets on the NLR data catalogue. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): BSD-3-Clause. Caveats: projections inherit sector model assumptions; data sets are large. Simulation uses: county-level hourly demand for capacity expansion and production cost models, electrification and demand response scenarios. Related records: model-resstock, model-comstock, model-reeds.
